learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the artistic secrets behind clothing design, mastering the elements of art and principles of design to create the perfect outfit!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Design is a plan for arranging elements in such a way that they fulfill a specific purpose. In apparel, structural design refers to how a garment is put together (seams, cuts), while applied design refers to surface decorations (embroidery, prints).
The building blocks of design are Line, Shape/Form (Silhouette), Color, and Texture. For example, vertical lines can make a person look taller, while horizontal lines can make them look wider.
These are the rules on how to use the elements. They include Balance (symmetry/asymmetry), Proportion (relationship of parts to the whole), Emphasis (focal point), Rhythm (flow), and Harmony.

Color is defined by three dimensions: Hue (the name of the color), Value (lightness or darkness, e.g., tints and shades), and Intensity (brightness or dullness). Warm colors advance, while cool colors recede.
The silhouette is the overall outline of a garment. It changes constantly with fashion trends—from the wide hoop skirts of the 1800s to the A-line dresses of the 1960s.

fun_activity.title: 📏 The Illusionist Wardrobe
fun_activity.instructions: Find a shirt with horizontal stripes and one with vertical stripes. Take a picture of yourself wearing both. Compare the photos—notice how the vertical stripes draw the eye up and down, making you look taller, while horizontal stripes draw the eye side-to-side!

exam_tips: 📌 Differentiate clearly between 'Elements of Design' (the tools) and 'Principles of Design' (how you use the tools).
📌 Remember the three dimensions of color: Hue, Value, and Intensity.
📌 Be able to explain the difference between Structural Design (essential to the garment) and Applied Design (purely decorative).
quick_recap: ⭐ The Color Wheel helps designers choose harmonious color schemes like monochromatic or complementary.
⭐ Texture affects how colors appear; a shiny fabric makes a color look lighter than a rough fabric of the same color.
⭐ Good design achieves Harmony, giving the feeling that all parts of an outfit belong together.
